programme: A neuroendocrine gland-specification network — ISL1 and NKX2-5 cross-regulate each other and sit upstream of NR2F1 (a direct NKX2-5 target); together with TTF1 (thyroid hormone synthesis genes TG, TPO, SLC5A5, DIO2), NR0B1/DAX1 (adrenal and gonadal steroidogenesis: STAR, CYP17A1, CYP11A1, NR5A1, FSHR, AMH, MC2R), IRF2BPL (the GnRH-kisspeptin pair GNRH1/KISS1) and ALX3 (islet hormones SST, INS), these factors target the hormone-synthesis and hormone-gene machinery of the thyroid, adrenal, gonadal and pancreatic-islet axes rather than any single organ.
role_in_a: In fibromyalgia this axis would be expected to surface as blunted or dysregulated HPA/thyroid/gonadal hormone output — a pattern consistent with fibromyalgia's known association with cortisol and thyroid axis abnormalities — but no Open Targets association or retrieved literature places any of these seven factors in fibromyalgia specifically; the role is expected from the biology of the axis, not documented here.
role_in_b: In psoriasis the same axis would be expected to act through skin's own peripheral steroidogenic and stress-hormone capacity, plausible given psoriasis's known links to stress and hormonal triggers, but again none of the seven factors carries an Open Targets association or a retrieved paper for psoriasis.
shared_axis: If a common thread exists, it is that both a chronic pain syndrome and a chronic inflammatory skin disease are sensitive to systemic and local neuroendocrine tone (HPA, thyroid, gonadal), so the same gland-specification transcription factors could be redeployed in blood and in skin as a shared stress/hormone-axis signature rather than as a tissue-identity artifact.
reasoning: The seven factors form a nameable programme purely from their target-gene architecture — thyroid, adrenal, gonadal and islet hormone genes, plus direct cross-targeting between ISL1, NKX2-5 and NR2F1 — so this is not an arbitrary list. But Open Targets records no association for any of the twelve factors in either disease, and the only retrieved paper (for HOXA10, not one of the carrying factors) is about endometriosis and not about fibromyalgia or psoriasis. The account therefore rests on developmental-biology reasoning about what the targets do, not on anything placed in either disease by the record.
support: none found; PMID 38674005 was retrieved for HOXA10 under fibromyalgia but its title and abstract concern endometriosis, not fibromyalgia, and HOXA10 is not among the carrying factors, so it does not bear on this claim.
how_to_falsify: In matched fibromyalgia and psoriasis cohorts, test whether blood/skin regulatory activity of NR0B1, TTF1, NR2F1, ISL1, NKX2-5 and IRF2BPL correlates with circulating cortisol, thyroid hormone, gonadotropin and kisspeptin levels; a genuine shared neuroendocrine axis predicts correlated dysregulation across that hormone panel in both diseases, while tissue-specific noise would not produce that correlation.
caveats: Blood (fibromyalgia) and skin (psoriasis) are not matched tissues, and the 32 patient-group comparisons are drawn from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the concordance rests on limited independent replication. All twelve factors lack any Open Targets association in either disease. The tissue-generic exclusion list removed AR, STAT1, STAT3, SPI1 and other classic immune/hormone-adjacent factors, which is why the surviving list reads as a specific developmental-endocrine signature rather than the generic blood/skin inflammatory story — but that also means the account is built entirely from target-gene inference, with no corroborating literature or database evidence behind it.
